questions.q:
Vineet, Rajesh and Kriti have different amount of money with them, Rajesh has just double the amount of money than Vineet. The total amount of money that Rajesh and Kriti have is Rs. 147. Kriti has Rs. 6 more than the amount Vineet has.

How much money does Kriti have?
questions.solution:
Suppose Vineet has Rs. x.

Rajesh has Rs. 2x.

Kriti has Rs. x + 6.

(2x) + (x + 6) = 147

3x + 6 = 147

3x = 141

x = 47

Vineet has Rs. 47.

Kriti has 47 + 6 = Rs. 53

Hence, 53 is the correct answer.

questions.q: In certain code language, ‘CAUGHT’ is coded as ‘326212087’. How will ‘SOLDER’ be coded as in that language?

The logic followed here is,

For C, U and H → Positional value of same letter → C = 3, U = 21 & H = 8

For A, G and T → Positional values of opposite letter → A = 26, G = 20 & T = 7

Therefore, CAUGHT → 326212087

Similarly,

For S, L and E → Positional value of same letter → S = 19, L = 12 & E = 5

For O, D and R → Positional values of opposite letter → O = 12, D = 23 & R = 9

Therefore, SOLDER → 1912122359

Hence, 1912122359 is the correct answer.

questions.q:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow from the statements:

Statements:

1. Some papers are copies

2. No copy is an eraser.

Conclusions:

I. Some copies are papers

II. Some papers are erasers.

III. No paper is an eraser.
options: Only Conclusion II and either conclusion I or III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.
Only conclusion I and either conclusion II or III follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.solution:
The logical Venn diagram according to given statements is,



Conclusions:

I. Some copies are papers → True (Some papers are copies)

II. Some papers are erasers. → False (it is possible but not definite)

III. No paper is an eraser. → False (it is possible but not definite)

Thus, II and III form a complementary pair.

Therefore, only conclusion I and either conclusion II or III follows.

Hence, option 3 is correct answer.

questions.q: Depreciation is an annual allowance for the wear and tear of .
questions.solution:
• Depreciation is an annual allowance for wear and tear of a capital good. In other words, it is the cost of the good divided by a number of years of its useful life.

• While calculating depreciation unexpected or sudden destruction or disuse of capital as can happen with accidents, natural calamities or other such extraneous circumstances are not taken into account.

• As an accounting term, depreciation is an expired cost or expense, charged against the revenue of a given accounting period.

• It is the diminution in the intrinsic value of the asset due to use and/or lapse of time.

questions.q: The total number of images formed by two mirrors inclined at 120° asymmetrically to each other is .
questions.solution:
CONCEPT:

Plane Mirror:

• A plane mirror is a mirror with a flat (planar) reflective surface.



The number of images formed when the object is placed between two plane mirrors:

⇒ θ = Angle between the two plane mirrors, and n = number of images formed

• If (360)/(θ) = even number

⇒ n=(360)/(θ)-1

• If (360)/(θ) = odd number and the object lies symmetrically

⇒ n=(360)/(θ)-1

• If (360)/(θ) = odd number and the object lies asymmetrically

⇒ n=(360)/(θ)

• If (360)/(θ) = fraction

⇒ n = only integer part of (360)/(θ)

CALCULATION:

Given that: θ = 120°

Number of images (n) = (360/120) = 3

So option 2 is correct.

​ Additional Information

• The first mirror was made by German Scientist Justus von Liebig. He coated the plane surface of a piece of ordinary glass with silver metal for making this mirror. Such a mirror is called a silvered glass mirror.

• Concave mirror: If the inner surface of the spherical mirror is the reflecting surface.

• Convex mirror: If the outer surface of the spherical mirror is the reflecting surface.

• List of Union Territories: 1. Andaman and Nicobar 2. Chandigarh 3. Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli 4. Delhi 5. Jammu and Kashmir 6. Ladakh 7. Lakshadweep 8. Puducherry

• Recently parliament has amended Article 240(1) of the Constitution to merge 2 UTs into one which will be called UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

• In August 2019 parliament passed the bill - Jammu and Kashmir (Reorganisation) Bill, 2019 which has removed Jammu and Kashmir's status of a state and converted it into 2 UTs - Jammu and Kashmir with a legislature and Ladakh without legislature.

questions.q: Reema sold 48 articles for Rs. 2,160 and suffered a loss of 10%. How many articles should she sell for Rs. 2,016 to earn a profit of 12%?
questions.solution:
SP of 48 articles = Rs. 2160

CP of 48 articles = 2160 × (100/90) = Rs. 2400

CP of 1 article = 2400/48 = Rs. 50

New sp of 1 article = 50 × (112/100) = 56

In Rs. 56 we can sold = 1 article

In Rs. 1 we can sold = 1/56 article

In Rs. 2016 we can sold = 1/56 × 2016 = 36 articles



Number of article = 2016/(2160/48 × 100/90 × 112/100)

Number of article = 2016/56 = 36 articles

questions.q: Diameter AB of a circle with centre O is produced to a point P such that PO = 16.8 cm. PQR is a secant that intersects the circle at Q and R such that PQ = 12 cm and PR = 19.2 cm. The length of AB (in cm) is:

From the following figure

Let the radius of the circle AO = OB = x, then

PA = (16.8 + x) and PB = (16.8 – x)

As we know,

PB × PA = PQ × PR

(16.8 – x) (16.8 + x) = 12 × 19.2

16.8² – x² = 12 × 19.2

x² = 16.8² – 12 × 19.2 = 12² (1.4² – 1.6) = 144 × (1.96 – 1.60)

x = √(144 × 0.36)

x = 7.2

Hence, 2x = 14.4

∴AB = 14.4

For easy calculation

Given,

Divided by 12, then

PO = 1.4, PQ = 1 and PR = 1.6

(1.4 – x) (1.4 + x) = 1 × 1.6

1.96 – x² = 1.6

x² = 0.36

x = √0.36

x = 0.6

2x = 1.2

AB = 1.2

Multiply by 12 in 1.2 and get correct answer = 1.2 × 12 = 14.4

questions.q: If the radius of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 10%, and the height is increased by 20%, then the percentage increase/decrease in its volume is:
questions.solution:
Ratio of volume before and after = 500 : 486

Again multiply by 2 in = 1000 : 972

Volume decreased by = 1000 – 972 = 28

As we know, 28 = 2.8%

Detailed Solution:

Let the radius of the cylinder be r cm and height of the cylinder be h cm,

As we know,

Volume of the cylinder = πr²h

New radius of the cylinder = r × (90/100) = 0.9r cm

New height of the cylinder = h × (120/100) = 1.2h cm

New volume of the cylinder = π × (0.9r)² × 1.2h = 0.81r² × 1.2h × π = 0.972rhπ

Required percentage = [(πr²h - 0.972πrh)/πrh] × 100 = 2.8%

questions.q: When a positive integer is divided by d, the remainder is 15. When ten times of the same number is divided by d, the remainder is 6. The least possible value of d is:
questions.solution:
Given:

When a positive number is divided by d, the remainder is 15

When ten times of the same number is divided by d, the remainder is 6

Calculation:

As given, Remainder is 15 so we can say the value of d is greater than 15. Only 16 and 18 is greater than 15.

Let us try with the least of the two options

Since the minimum value for the positive number, for 15 to be remainder when divided by 16 = 31

Ten times of 31 = 310

310/16 → 6 (remainder)

Since from there only we got the solution, we need not check for 18 as it is asked for the least value of d.

So the value of d is 16.

So, the rectified sentence is: No fewer than fifty participants were present for the singing competition.

The old man did not wanted to eat any food.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e., did not wanted.

Whenever a sentence uses the verb form 'did', the corresponding verb must not use the past tense form of the verb.

As 'did' already represents the past tense, using past tense form of the verb, viz, here, 'wanted', is redundant.

So, the corrected sentence is: The old man did not want to eat any food.

He greeted his friend and asked what he could do for him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4, i.e., He greeted his friend and asked what he could do for him.

While converting greetings like 'Hello' or 'Hi' to indirect speech, the main verb becomes 'greeted'.

The 'wh-questions', when turned to indirect speech, turn the main verb into 'asked'.

So, the correct indirect speech would be: He greeted his friend and asked what he could do for him.

questions.q:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

They are constructing a residential youth hostel.
options: A residential youth hostel is being constructed by them.
A residential youth hostel was constructed by them.
A residential youth hostel has been constructed by them.
A residential youth hostel is constructed by them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e., A residential youth hostel is being constructed by them.

The rule for changing the voice from active to passive is: Subject and object change places and the main verb is changed to past participle form+ forms of 'to be', as per the tense.

Here, the subject 'They' becomes the object, viz, the passive form of 'they', viz., 'them'.

The object 'a residential youth hostel' becomes the subject.

The verb is in present continuous tense, so it changes to: 'being constructed'.

The passive form, thus becomes: A residential youth hostel is being constructed by them.

questions.q:
Direction: Select the correct antonym of the given word.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Repulse.'

Key Points

• 'Allure' means *powerfully attract or charm; tempt*.

• 'Allure' का अर्थ है शक्तिशाली रूप से आकर्षित या आकर्षण; लुभाना।

• Example: *Will sponsors really be allured by such opportunities?*

• Let us explore the meanings of the given words:

• Repulse- cause to feel intense distaste and aversion. (तीव्र अरुचि और घृणा महसूस करना।)

• Attract- cause to come to a place or participate in a venture by offering something of interest or advantage. (किसी स्थान पर आने या किसी उद्यम में रुचि या लाभ की पेशकश करके भाग लेना।)

• Revive- restore to life or consciousness. (जीवन या चेतना को बहाल करना।)

• Hence, we can say that the correct antonym of the given word 'Allure' is 'Repulse.'

• Therefore, the correct answer is 'Repulse.'

questions.q:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

A. Although I had a fear of water, I thought it was an important skill I should learn.

B. However, what I didn't realize was that it would also make me a more confident person.

C. I also thought it would be a good exercise that would make me physically stronger.

D. One of the hardest things I've had to do was to learn how to swim.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is DACB.

Key Points

• The given sentence is an example of a Sentence Jumble.

• The first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, the starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.

• Part D will be the first sentence because it is an independent statement. It mentions about 'one of the hardest things of a person's life'.

• Part A will be the next in sequence. It has 'although'. You use although to introduce a subordinate clause that contains a statement that contrasts with the statement in the main clause. It mentions the reason behind the speaker learning how to swim despite having fear of water.

• Part C will be the next in sequence. It has 'also' and states another reason behind learning how to swim.

• Part B will be the next in sequence. It has 'However'. You use however when you are adding a comment which is surprising or which contrasts with what has just been said. It mentions that the speaker later realized that it helped in increasing confidence.

Thus, the sentences will be arranged as: *One of the hardest things I've had to do was to learn how to swim. Although I had a fear of water, I thought it was an important skill I should learn. I also thought it would be a good exercise that would make me physically stronger. However, what I didn't realize was that it would also make me a more confident person.*
